rationale: The feature is a new change-level decomposition stage plus recursive nested runStart invocations, all inside the existing sdd-runner workspace. Core touch points: (1) events.ts owns StageIdSchema/STAGE_ORDER and the L2 event vocabulary — a new pipeline stage and nested-run spawn/aggregate events cascade into every STAGE_ORDER consumer (stage-machine.ts remainingStages, replay.ts fold, renderer/watch-view/run-view TUI); (2) orchestrator.ts composes intake→draft→review→decompose→atomicity→gate for exactly one change (runPlanningStages) and must gain a parent stage that validates a decomposition, spawns child runs per decomposed change, and aggregates their outcomes; (3) run-state.ts PersistedRunStateSchema needs parent/child run linkage, recursion depth, and cross-run budget state; (4) intake.ts depth classification (S/M/L signals) is where 'task too large' routing originates; (5) decompose.ts already implements task-granularity split/merge with agent+validateStrict retry — the change-granularity analogue is a new sibling module (change-decompose.ts), not an edit of it; (6) openspec-driver.ts must create/validate multiple sibling changes per run; (7) gate machinery (gate.ts, auto-policy.ts R1–R5, extend-round.ts, post-review-tail.ts) is affected because child runs gate independently and the R4 budget guard must see aggregate nested spend; (8) resume/routing surfaces (resume-flow.ts, resume-decision.ts, continue.ts, cli-routing.ts, cli.ts) assume flat single-change runs; (9) config.ts rejects unknown keys strictly, so any recursion-limit/budget-sharing knobs are schema changes. No SQLite involvement (run state is JSON files under workDir) so no db migration; no chat/task provider or credential surface is touched. Novelty judged structurally: no new top-level module — the work extends existing orchestrator/events/state/gate modules of sdd-runner with one or two new files inside it.
